title: From the unit circle to the sine wave
examples: How does the unit circle make the sine graph?
Why does the sine graph repeat?

marks.label: 360°: back to 0
marks.ask: Why does the sine graph repeat?

explain.say: Imagine riding a Ferris wheel, like the London Eye, with a radius of 1 unit. Start level with the centre. As the wheel turns, your height goes up and down. This wave is your height above the centre. That height is called sine of the angle.

draw.text: From the unit circle to the sine wave

marks.label: 360°: back to 0
marks.ask: Why does the sine graph repeat?

explain.say: After a quarter turn, 90 degrees, you are at the very top. Your height is the full radius, 1. Look at the yellow mark: sine of 90 degrees is 1. Can you feel how high you are?

marks.label: 360°: back to 0
marks.ask: Why does the sine graph repeat?

explain.say: Keep turning to 180 degrees, half way round. You are level with the centre again, so the height is 0. Look at the cyan mark. You are on the other side now.

marks.label: 360°: back to 0
marks.ask: Why does the sine graph repeat?

explain.say: At 270 degrees you are at the bottom, 1 unit below the centre. Below means negative, so sine is minus 1: the purple mark. Then at 360 degrees you are back where you began, the orange mark. What do you think happens next?

marks.label: 360°: back to 0
marks.ask: Why does the sine graph repeat?

explain.say: It all repeats! Every full turn draws the same wave again. Well done! This wave is everywhere: sound, light, tides and the electricity in your home, which wiggles 50 or 60 times every second.

faq.q: How does the unit circle make the sine graph?
faq.a: A point goes round a circle of radius 1. Its height above the centre is sine of the angle. Plot that height against the angle and you draw the sine wave.
At 90 degrees the point is at the very top of the unit circle, a full radius above the centre. The radius is 1, so the height, sine, is 1.
Below the centre of the circle the height is negative. Between 180 and 360 degrees the point is underneath, so sine is negative there.

faq.q: Why does the sine graph repeat?
faq.a: After a full turn of 360 degrees the point is back where it started, so the heights repeat. The sine wave has a period of 360 degrees.
asks: What is the period of sine?

faq.a: Cosine is the sideways distance of the point from the centre. Its graph is the same wave as sine, just shifted by 90 degrees.
asks: What is cosine on the unit circle?

facts: On the unit circle, the point at angle θ has coordinates (cos θ, sin θ).
The sine function has a period of 360°, which is 2π radians.

quiz.why: At 270° the point is at the bottom of the unit circle, 1 below the centre.

quiz.say: After how many degrees does the sine wave repeat?

quiz.why: One full turn brings the point back to the start.
